label: E_b
prompt:
A restaurant emailed a PDF invoice but it never showed up. List the reasons this can happen and where each error is recorded.

Do not edit files. Answer concisely with file:line references.
answer:
Inbound invoice emails are processed by `InvoiceEmailService.handleEmail`. A scheduled job, `ParseInvoiceEmailsJob.java:22`, calls it. Each failure is recorded in one of two places:

- **`emailReceivingRecord` table:** entity `EmailReceivingRecord.java:15-30`, `errors` column. `InvoiceEmailService.java:166` saves it, and `getErrors` at `:243` reads it back.
- **OrderlyLogger:** tag `InvoiceEmail` (`:58`) or an exception log.

| # | Reason | Where recorded |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The recipient address has no local part that matches a restaurant id (for example, not `1234@invoices.gotorderly.com`). | `errors` text "We could not find an email that looked like it was addressed to us…" (`InvoiceEmailService.java:163`). The S3 file is moved to `noLocalPart/`. |
| 2 | The local part is not a known restaurant id, or the id isn't numeric. `getRestaurantFromAddresses` swallows that exception on purpose (`:200-202`). | `errors` text "<localPart> was not a known rest id…" (`:160`). The S3 file is moved to `unknown/<localPart>/`. |
| 3 | The restaurant is inactive. | `errors` text "Restaurant was not marked active" (`:124-126`). |
| 4 | The attachment is neither an image/PDF nor a CSV/TXT file (`:52-53`, `:141`). The check is by file extension only, so a PDF with no `.pdf` suffix fails here. | `errors` text "<name> was not image or text type file" (`:141`). |
| 5 | A CSV/TXT attachment came from a sender domain that isn't in `supplierDomainMapping`. Only `rnc.sysco.com` is mapped (`:69`, `:138`). This doesn't apply to PDFs. | `errors` text "<name> did not have a supplier mapping." (`:138`). |
| 6 | Saving the attachment threw an exception, in `saveNewGroupingForInvoice` or `addInvoiceAttachment` (`:129-130`). | `errors` text "<name> -- <message>" (`:144`). |
| 7 | The recipient headers (to/cc/bcc) couldn't be read. | `errors` text in `InvoiceRecipientResolver.java:76`. |
| 8 | The MIME message couldn't be parsed. `EmailParser.java:51` throws "Failed to parse email". When this surfaces as `UnparsableMessageException`, the file goes to S3 `unparsable/`. | OrderlyLogger exception log with the `s3Key` (`:182`). **No DB record is written.** |
| 9 | Any other exception in `handleEmail` (`:167-169`) or while moving the S3 file (`:184-185`). The email stays under `invoices/` and is retried on the next run. | OrderlyLogger exception log with `failedEmailFile` or `s3Key`. **No DB record is written.** |
| 10 | The job doesn't run in dev (`:91-93`). | Not recorded. |

For a PDF that is missing from the app, check these first:

- Look for a row in `emailReceivingRecord` where `allAttachments` lists the PDF but `attachmentsMoved` doesn't. The `errors` column says why.
- If there is no row, look in the S3 `unparsable/` folder and in the logs under the `InvoiceEmail` tag. That points to reasons 8 or 9.

I didn't trace where `UnparsableMessageException` is thrown, so the exact trigger for reason 8 is unconfirmed.
